newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy finance ministry to meet on budget measures.
newsitem.headline: Italy finance ministry to meet on budget measures.

text.p: Officials at the Italian finance ministry are due to meet on Friday to put the finishing touches to a year-end package of measures which form the last part of the 1997 budget still to be fully worked out.
The measures, which are meant to raise around 4.3 trillion lire out of the total budget worth 62.5 trillion lire, are due to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Monday.

As part of the provisions, the finance ministry is expected to extend a tax hike on petrol introduced last year to help pay for Italy's peace-keeping force in Bosnia. An extension of the 22 lire per litre hike would bring in some 250 billion lire in 1997, state television RAI said on Thursday.
Among other provisions widely expected in the end-of-year package are an increase in duty on cigarettes and an anticipation of some tax payments.
RAI said this last measure could raise up to two trillion lire and newspapers reported that petrol stations might be among the bodies which are given less time to pay their taxes.

Petrol stations on Tuesday announced a four-day strike for December 29 and January 3 to protest against the reported changes. Petrol firm representatives are due to meet industry ministry officials on Friday to discuss the situation.

Italian media also said earlier this week that the government was studying plans to increase taxes on cellular phones as well as lift the price of instant lottery tickets, however the finance ministry on Tuesday dismissed the reports.
The 1997 budget has already been approved by parliament and the end-of-year measures will enter into immediate effect without recourse to parliament.
